timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: If ransomware hits, we just restore from backup, right?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Only if the backups survived, the credentials are clean, and the restore plan was tested.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Of course. Deleting backups is how they increase pressure to pay.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So what is the architecture answer?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Immutable backups, isolated recovery credentials, separate admin paths, and prioritized restoration tiers.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Restore identity, networking, security monitoring, and critical business systems before nice-to-have services.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Regularly. Tabletop exercises are good. Actual restore drills are better.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Patching reduces entry points. Recovery architecture limits blast radius when prevention fails.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. Hope is not a recovery time objective.
